title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (previous page). Grothendieck considers elliptic curves E over a field k of characteristic not 2, with a 'Legendre–Jacobi pinning of level 2'. He has shown that the groupoid of such pinned curves is equivalent to the groupoid of triples (J, t, α):
- J is a 3-element set, the non-zero 2-torsion points.
- t is a point of Σ_J^*(k), where Σ_J is the projective line attached to J, minus the three points of J.
- α : ω_J ≅ μ_4^* is an identification. Here ω_J is the 2-element set (quadratic torsor) attached to J, and μ_4^* is the set of primitive 4th roots of unity, i.e. the square roots of −1.
A Jacobi pinning (a bijection J ≅ {0,1,∞}) identifies Σ_J with P^1_k and makes ω_J ≅ ω_{0,1,∞} canonically pointed. The Legendre datum α then amounts to choosing a square root i of −1, the 'arithmetic' datum.

This page.
- Line 1 finishes the statement. The groupoid of elliptic curves with a Legendre–Jacobi pinning is rigid (no non-trivial automorphisms; the −1 automorphism is killed by α). It is equivalent to the discrete set of pairs (t, i), with t ∈ U_{0,3}(k) = P^1(k) \ {0,1,∞} and i ∈ μ_4^*(k).
- In modern terms, the stack M(2) over Z[1/2] is a μ_2-gerbe over P^1 − {0,1,∞}. It is rigidified, and in fact trivialised, by adding a μ_4^*-valued datum. The fine moduli space is then (P^1 − {0,1,∞}) × μ_4^*, i.e. (P^1 − {0,1,∞}) over Z[1/2, i].
- A crossed-out attempt defines a twisted line bundle O_{Σ_J}(1)^♮ = O_{Σ_J}(1) ∧^{μ_4} (something).
- He then moves to an arbitrary base S over S_0 = Spec Z[1/2] (residue characteristics ≠ 2).
- Given a fixed μ_4-torsor Q_0 over S_0, he defines for sheaves M of μ_4-modules (e.g. O_S-modules, μ_4 acting through μ_4 ⊂ G_m) the twist (22): M^♮ = M ∧^{μ_4} Q_0. Equivalently M^♮ ≅ M ⊗ O_S^♮, where O_S^♮ is the invertible sheaf obtained by pushing Q_0 out along μ_4 → G_m.
- (23): M^♮ ⊗ M^♮ ≅ M^♭ := M ∧^{μ_2} μ_4^*. This holds because on M⊗M the group μ_4 acts through squaring μ_4 → μ_2, and the induced μ_2-torsor Q_0^{(2)} is identified with μ_4^*.
- (24): μ_4^* = μ_4 \ μ_2 is a μ_2-torsor, i.e. the étale double cover Spec Z[1/2, i] of S_0.
- The natural (implicit) choice of Q_0 is the scheme of primitive 8th roots of unity, {x : x^4 = −1}. It is a μ_4-torsor whose image under squaring is {y : y^2 = −1} = μ_4^*.

Purpose (next page). For an étale cubic cover J/S, take Σ_J = P(V_J), with V_J the trace-zero quotient of p_*O_J. The twist T_0 = O_{Σ_J}(1)^♮ is a twisted square root of the tangent bundle: T_0^{⊗2} ≅ T_{Σ_J} ∧ (μ_4^* ∧ ω_J). This is applied to Σ_J = E/±1 with J = (₂E)^*. It is a canonical 'twisted theta characteristic' on the quotient line E/±1, presumably to relate it to Lie(E) or ω_E and to get a canonical, base-independent form of the Legendre model.
errors: No mathematical errors visible. Q_0 is not defined on this page; (23) requires Q_0^{(2)} ≅ μ_4^* as μ_2-torsors, which holds for Q_0 = μ_8^* (x^4 = −1) but needs to be specified.
Minor: M^♭ is written as M ∧^{μ_2} μ_4^*, but M⊗M (not M) is what carries the μ_2-action through squaring. The notation implicitly regards M⊗M, or a module with μ_4-action factoring through μ_2.

ideas.what: Elliptic curves with Legendre–Jacobi level-2 pinning form a rigid groupoid equivalent to pairs (t,i), t ∈ P^1−{0,1,∞}, i² = −1. The −1 automorphism is killed by an arithmetic datum (a square root of −1) rather than by a differential.
ideas.modern_name: Rigidification/trivialisation of the μ_2-gerbe M(2) → P^1−{0,1,∞} (Legendre family)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical Legendre family; moduli-stack form Deligne–Rapoport (1973), Katz–Mazur (1985)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses M_{1,1}, level structures and P^1−{0,1,∞}, but not this explicit pinning

ideas.what: Twisting μ_4-module sheaves by a μ_4-torsor Q_0 over Spec Z[1/2] (primitive 8th roots of unity), whose square is the μ_2-torsor μ_4^* of square roots of −1.
ideas.modern_name: Contracted product / twisting by a torsor; 'half twist' by μ_8 over Z[1/2]
ideas.where_published: Contracted product formalism: SGA 1, SGA 3, Giraud's Cohomologie non abélienne; this specific twist: no

ideas.what: Twisted square root of the tangent bundle of Σ_J = P(V_J) ≅ E/±1, needing the arithmetic twist by μ_4^* and the discriminant torsor ω_J (next page, eq. 26–27).
ideas.modern_name: Canonical (twisted) theta characteristic / spin structure on the conic E/±1 over Z[1/2]

missed.claim: The canonical 'square root' of the tangent bundle of E/±1 over Z[1/2] requires twisting by the μ_8-torsor of primitive 8th roots of unity, with square the torsor of √−1. This links level-2 moduli to the arithmetic 8th roots of unity familiar from theta transformation formulas and metaplectic (weight 1/2) phenomena. The notes do not draw this link explicitly; it is implied.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a scheme-theoretic, base-independent origin of the ζ_8 factors in theta multipliers. It may interest people working on integral models of metaplectic or theta line bundles over the Legendre/level-2 moduli. This is likely known in spirit, though not in this formulation.

missed.claim: The programme of giving an intrinsic, descent-friendly version of the Legendre normal form over any base over Z[1/2] via (J, t, α) and twisted line bundles on Σ_J ≅ E/±1. It is begun here and continued over the following pages.
missed.quote: Je suppose : une base quelconque, mais je travaille en car. rés. ≠ 2 i.e. sur la base absolue S_0 = Spec(Z[1/2])
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an explicit, canonical rigidification of M(2) with arithmetic data. Similar constructions exist in the literature (Katz–Mazur, explicit level-2 models), so its novelty is modest.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but essentially standard torsor-twisting setup. The rigidification by a √−1 datum and the μ_8 twist are neat and somewhat unusual in presentation, but the underlying facts about the Legendre family and M(2) are well known.
transcription_corrections: First line likely reads 'est équivalente :' (to the set of couples) rather than 'est isomorphe'.
In (22) the torsor is written Q_{0S} (base change of Q_0 to S); the extra crossed-out mark below it is a deletion.
